newsitem.title: USA: USDA food safety chief Taylor to quit -- official.
newsitem.headline: USDA food safety chief Taylor to quit -- official.

text.p: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) Administrator Michael Taylor will resign effective at the end of the year, a U.S. administration official said Wednesday.
An announcement from the White House or from USDA on Taylor's resignation was imminent, the official, who declined to be named, said.
Taylor was instrumental in drawing up and getting approval for revolutionary new regulations to improve U.S. meat and poultry inspection, which were published July 27.
The rules are to be implemented over the next two-and-a-half years.
Jacque Knight, a spokeswoman for Taylor, would not confirm Taylor's resignation. "I have no official statement," Knight said.

As well as being administrator of FSIS since August 1994, Taylor has also been acting Undersecretary for Food Safety since October 1994. That appointment was never sent to the Senate for confirmation.
